concepts.en: Where in the world am I?

summary.big_en: Unit 1 is about identity: the feelings we share, where we are in the world, and the people we admire.

words.title: Feelings and how we judge words

items.def: To come first in a game or competition.
items.example: A positive word in the Connections game (p.13).

items.def: To hurt or frighten someone weaker, again and again.
items.example: A negative word in the Connections game (p.13).

items.def: Very good indeed.
items.example: A positive word in the Connections game (p.13).

items.def: Unkind to other people.
items.example: A negative word in the Connections game (p.13).

items.def: Damage or injury done to someone or something.
items.example: A negative word in the Connections game (p.13).

items.def: To suffer or die because there is no food.
items.example: A negative word in the Connections game (p.13).

words.note: Activity 6 asks you to sort these words into positive and negative, and say how you know.

items.def: The most northern or the most southern point of the Earth.
items.example: At one end is the North Pole and at the other, the South Pole (p.15).

items.def: A unit of measurement.
items.example: The equator's line of latitude is zero degrees (p.15).

items.def: Two lines that stay the same distance apart.
items.example: Lines of latitude circle the Earth parallel to the equator (p.15).

items.def: Standing upwards.
items.example: Lines of longitude divide the Earth into vertical sections (p.15).

items.def: A code that shows an exact position on a map.
items.example: Bangkok is at 13° N 100° E (p.15).

items.def: A person who takes action to support their beliefs.
items.example: Malala Yousafzai is an activist for girls' education (p.16).

items.def: To think very well of someone.
items.example: Aliya explains why she admires Malala (p.16).

items.def: To refuse to allow something.
items.example: Girls were banned from going to school (p.16).

items.def: The internet, newspapers, TV and magazines.
items.example: Malala's story was reported in the media (p.16).

items.def: To disagree and complain very strongly.
items.example: People protested when the school was closed (p.16).

items.def: To organise activities to achieve something.
items.example: Malala campaigns for girls' education (p.16).

words.title: Adjectives and their noun forms

items.def: So surprising that you can hardly believe it.
items.example: I looked at it in amazement (p.18).

items.def: Making you feel happy and full of energy.
items.example: I remember that feeling of excitement very well (p.18).

items.def: Making you feel very frightened.
items.example: It was exciting and terrifying at the same time (p.18).

items.def: Pleased about something good you have done.
items.example: I felt a sense of pride for doing something brave (p.18).

items.def: Pleased because you got what you wanted.
items.example: I felt very satisfied because I had achieved something big (p.18).

words.note: Activity 4 on the review page asks for the noun form of each of these adjectives (p.26).

items.def: Shaped like a bird's beak.
items.example: … that my nose would be on the beaky side (p.20).

items.def: To move quickly with a short, light movement.
items.example: … white-blond hair that flicks around my face (p.20).

items.def: Not like most others; not common.
items.example: The unit ends with a story about a girl with an unusual name (p.11).

grammar.title: Present perfect
grammar.when: Use the present perfect for events in the recent past, when the time of the event is not important.

examples.why: the drawing is finished; when is not the point
question form: have + subject + past participle

examples.en: I have never been afraid of water again.
examples.why: an experience that covers up to now

examples.en: But I haven't been on a rollercoaster again!

grammar.watch: Ask 'Have you ever…?' when you want to know about someone's experience (p.19).

grammar.title: Prepositions before nouns
grammar.when: A preposition shows the connection between nouns and adjectives in a sentence.

examples.en: Lines of longitude run from the North Pole to the South Pole.
… one of the hottest places on our planet

grammar.title: verb + direct object + infinitive
grammar.when: Some verbs take a person first and then an infinitive with 'to'.

examples.en: My friend asked me to go with him.
My dad taught me to swim.

grammar.watch: Activity 5 asks you to find another example of this pattern in Cody's description (p.19).

readings.title: Geography: how we map the Earth
readings.about: Lines of latitude circle the Earth parallel to the equator and lines of longitude run pole to pole, so any place can be given as a coordinate.

readings.title: Aliya's presentation about Malala Yousafzai
readings.about: Aliya explains why she chose Malala, tells her early life and her work, and ends by saying why she admires her.

readings.title: First-time experiences
readings.about: Santok rode a rollercoaster, Olivia saw the sea, and Cody learned to swim; each says what happened and how it felt.

readings.title: A Girl Called Owl, by Amy Wilson
readings.about: A girl called Owl explains how she got her unusual name and how her own features seem to match it.

flashcards.front_en: When do you use the present perfect?
flashcards.back_en: For recent events when the exact time does not matter. Form: have or has + past participle.

flashcards.front_en: How do you ask about someone's experience?
flashcards.back_en: Have you ever…? — for example, Have you ever felt really proud of yourself?

flashcards.front_en: Latitude or longitude: which runs pole to pole?
flashcards.back_en: Longitude. Latitude circles the Earth parallel to the equator.

flashcards.front_en: How far apart are the lines of latitude?
flashcards.back_en: About 111 km, and each distance is measured in degrees.

flashcards.front_en: Three sequencing phrases for a presentation?
flashcards.back_en: Today, I'm going to talk about… / As I said in my introduction… / To sum up…

flashcards.front_en: What sound do -tion and -sion words end with?
flashcards.back_en: The same 'shun' sound: introduction, education, decision, presentation.

flashcards.front_en: Noun forms of proud, amazing, exciting?
Give an example of verb + object + infinitive.
flashcards.back_en: My dad taught me to swim. / My friend asked me to go with him.
The things that make you who you are.

flashcards.back_en: Lines that run from the North Pole to the South Pole.
The imaginary line circling the Earth halfway between the poles.

quiz.stem_en: Complete the question: '___ you finished yet?'
quiz.why_en: Present perfect question with 'you' uses 'have' (p.13).

quiz.stem_en: Complete: 'Why ___ you drawn a football?'
quiz.why_en: The present perfect uses have or has with the past participle (p.13).

quiz.stem_en: Which sentence is in the present perfect?
quiz.why_en: Present perfect is have or has plus the past participle (p.13).

quiz.stem_en: Why does 'I have drawn a car' use the present perfect and not the past simple?

choices.en: The event happened a very long time ago
The event has not happened yet
The event is recent and the exact time does not matter

quiz.why_en: We use the present perfect for recent events when the time is not important (p.13).

quiz.stem_en: Complete the negative: 'I ___ been on a rollercoaster again!'
quiz.why_en: The negative present perfect is have not plus the past participle (p.18).

quiz.stem_en: Which question asks about someone's experience?

choices.en: Have you ever felt really proud of yourself?

quiz.why_en: 'Have you ever…?' asks about experience up to now (p.19).

quiz.stem_en: Choose the correct preposition: '… places ___ our planet'
quiz.why_en: The text uses 'places on our planet' (p.14).

quiz.stem_en: Complete: 'Lines of latitude circle the Earth ___ to the equator.'
quiz.why_en: They are parallel to the equator (p.15).

quiz.stem_en: Complete: 'Lines of longitude run ___ the North Pole ___ the South Pole.'
quiz.why_en: The text uses from … to with the two poles (p.15).

quiz.stem_en: Which sentence follows the pattern verb + object + infinitive?

choices.en: My dad is a good swimmer.
My dad taught me to swim.

quiz.why_en: taught + me + to swim is verb + direct object + infinitive (p.18).

quiz.stem_en: Rewrite with the same pattern: 'My friend said I should go with him.' becomes:

choices.en: My friend asked going with him.
My friend asked me to go with him.
My friend asked that I go.

quiz.why_en: asked + me + to go matches the pattern in the text (p.18).

quiz.stem_en: A person who takes action to support their beliefs is called:
quiz.why_en: That is the definition matched in Activity 6 (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: 'To refuse to allow something' is the meaning of:
quiz.why_en: ban means to refuse to allow something (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: Complete: 'She works hard, so I really ___ her.'
quiz.why_en: admire means to think very well of someone (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: The internet, newspapers, TV and magazines are together called:
quiz.why_en: That is the definition given in Activity 6 (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: Which of these words is negative?
quiz.why_en: Activity 6 asks you to sort these words; bully is negative (p.13).

quiz.stem_en: What is a coordinate?

choices.en: A code that shows an exact position on a map
A line that circles the Earth
The most northern point of the Earth

quiz.why_en: A coordinate is a code to show exact positions on a map (p.15).

quiz.stem_en: What does 'vertical' mean?
quiz.why_en: The key words box gives 'standing upwards' (p.15).

quiz.stem_en: What is the noun form of the adjective 'proud'?
quiz.why_en: Activity 4 on the review page asks for these noun forms (p.19, p.26).

quiz.stem_en: What is the noun form of the adjective 'amazing'?
quiz.why_en: Olivia's text uses 'I looked at it in amazement' (p.18).

quiz.stem_en: The equator circles the Earth halfway between the poles. What is its line of latitude?
quiz.why_en: Its line of latitude is zero degrees (p.15).

quiz.stem_en: Lines of latitude are about the same distance apart. How far apart are they?
quiz.why_en: They are the same distance apart, about 111 km (p.15).

quiz.stem_en: Latitude is measured 0–90° north and south. How far is longitude measured east and west?
quiz.why_en: Lines of longitude are measured 0–180° east and west (p.15).

quiz.stem_en: What happens when a place lies between the lines on a map?

choices.en: The place cannot be given a coordinate
You round to the nearest whole degree
You use the nearest city instead
The degrees are divided into minutes and seconds

quiz.why_en: We divide the degrees into minutes and seconds (p.15).

quiz.stem_en: Which phrase would you use to START a presentation?

choices.en: Today, I'm going to talk about…
To sum up, I chose to…
Since then, with her father, she…

quiz.why_en: The speaking tip box lists this as an opening phrase (p.17).

quiz.stem_en: Which phrase would you use to FINISH a presentation?

choices.en: Today, I'm going to talk about…
To sum up, I chose to…
As I said in my introduction…

quiz.why_en: 'To sum up' comes at the end (p.17).

quiz.stem_en: Why do you use sequencing words in a presentation?

choices.en: They make the words sound nicer
They help the audience follow the order of your ideas
They replace the need for facts

quiz.why_en: Use sequencing words to help your audience follow your presentation (p.17).

quiz.stem_en: Listen to the words introduction, education, decision and presentation. What do they have in common?

choices.en: They are all names of people
They all start with the same sound
They all end with the same -tion or -sion sound

quiz.why_en: Activity 7 is a pronunciation task on -tion and -sion endings (p.17).

quiz.stem_en: Santok says the rollercoaster was 'exciting and terrifying at the same time'. What does this show?

choices.en: One experience can bring two opposite feelings at once
He did not enjoy any part of it
He had ridden one many times before

quiz.why_en: Santok describes both feelings in the same sentence (p.18).

quiz.stem_en: In A Girl Called Owl, why does the narrator think her name suits her?

choices.en: She keeps an owl as a pet
Her hair flicks like feathers and her nose is on the beaky side
She is very good at flying kites

quiz.why_en: She describes her hair and nose in the extract (p.20).
